wording: Consciousness is studied under several distinct concepts, including Nagel's 'what it is like' (phenomenal) sense and an access sense concerning availability of states to other mental processes.
locator: §§ on 'What it is like' and 'Access consciousness'

wording: Major neuroscientific theories include higher-order, global workspace, re-entry/predictive-processing and integrated information theories, which differ in explanatory targets and neural commitments.
Global Neuronal Workspace research proposes late amplification, long-range synchronization and prefronto-parietal 'ignition' as markers of conscious access.
counterevidence_limits: S18 reports a general lack of ignition at stimulus offset.

wording: A preregistered adversarial test (n = 256; fMRI, MEG, iEEG) found results aligned with some predictions of IIT and GNWT while substantially challenging key tenets of both.

In SIM-R5-C0, a single recurrent rate unit showed all-or-none sustained activity under strong recurrence (ignition fraction rose from <10% to >90% between amplitudes 1.8 and 2.8) and none under weak recurrence; this is a dynamical toy and says nothing about phenomenal experience.
counterevidence_limits: Bistability is generic to many non-conscious systems.

wording: No theory has been shown to resolve the phenomenal ('hard') aspect of consciousness.
